text:
mira: Anyone seeing a bunch of nodes in eu-west gone OOB-unavailable after the overnight BIOS push? We lost ~18 GPUs from the pool.

infra-bot: Deployment report: bios-fw-v2.4.1 applied to 42 hosts in eu-west-1. 18 marked degraded; 6 moved to maintenance. See /deploys/1975123456 for full list. :warning:

ashley: I grabbed BMC logs — several units tripped into a thermal-failsafe state and I can see the BMC toggling SecureBoot to 'Allow' then re-flashing boot order. That sequence is leaving some nodes in an EFI shell instead of PXE.

kai: Can you paste the ipmi sensors or a short journal snippet? Curious if it's an actual temperature spike or a false-positive power-scaling flag.

mira: Snippet from one node:```sh
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.2.7.12 -U admin -P **** sensor | egrep 'Temp|Sys Temp'
CPU Temp        | 38 degrees C  | ok
FPS Temp        | 82 degrees C  | ns
System Temp     | 45 degrees C  | ok
```

sam: That FPS/PCI temp reading looks bogus — vendor kernel patch in this BIOS changed sensor mapping so sensor ID 0x1a now reports PCI temp but units mis-scale -> thermal trip. When BMC goes into failsafe some firmwares flip BootFlags to make network the first device, but the PXE stack errors and machine falls to local EFI shell. It's a provisioning loop.

ashley: Quick triage I ran on a single node: `racadm set bios.biosconfig BootMode UEFI` then `racadm set secureboot.Enable 1` and power-cycle. Node rejoined after re-provision and GPU pool came back. Workaround works but it's manual and risky across 18 hosts. :thumbsup:

kai: We should pause the rollout immediately. If we evict Dedicated capacity to cover this we might hit commit shortfalls and trigger overage pricing. Need to weigh spinning temporary on-demand hosts vs slower rollback.

oncall: Oncall here — I'm pausing the rest of the rollout. Spinning up 8 spare GPU hosts in us-west to cover immediate load. Cost impact: ~USD 3k/day if we keep them for 72h. Proceed? :eyes:

mira: Proceed with spares, yes. Also open an incident and vendor ticket. I'm adding an ops runbook entry: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/bmc-bios-thermal (draft).

ashley: Sending vendor logs now. FRU and IPMI dumps attached to INC-7892. Vendor says they see a sensor-ID remap in the firmware that triggers ACPI thermal events when the GPU power table is adjusted. They're preparing a hotfix.

sam: For immediate mitigation we should: 1) disable the buggy sensor in BMC config (where possible) 2) enforce secureboot on affected image to avoid boot-order flip 3) add a watchdog extension so the node doesn't drop to maintenance on transient sensor blips. I can script 1+2 but need maint window for mass changes.

kai: Also add a safeguard to the rollout pipeline: after bios apply, run an automated `ipmitool sensor` validation and abort if any sensor shows 'ns' or 'nr' state in critical channels. Save us from fast-failing thousands of requests.

mira: Sounds good. I'll coordinate with Product to throttle active allocations while we move workloads to spares. We'll keep the rest of the fleet paused until vendor hotfix or we confirm safe sensor mapping. I'll update INC-7892 and post status soon. :white_check_mark:
